learnings: Persistence is real but mostly in the cash prices, not in futures: monthly announced price changes have autocorrelation Class III milk 0.13, Class IV milk 0.42, Cheese 0.13, Butter 0.29, Nonfat dry milk 0.49, Dry whey 0.68 (an average of a random walk alone gives about 0.25); weekly futures returns have Class III milk 0.06, Class IV milk 0.12, Cheese 0.08, Butter 0.07, Nonfat dry milk 0.17, Dry whey -0.07. Futures already price most of the cash persistence.

Class III milk: best forecast of the futures error is 'Fitted share of (cash + seasonal) gap' (out-of-sample R² -3.6% vs the futures price, right on direction 41.1% of the time, month-clustered t -2.81).

Class IV milk: best forecast of the futures error is 'Fitted share of (cash + seasonal) gap' (out-of-sample R² -5.8% vs the futures price, right on direction 50.6% of the time, month-clustered t 0.74).
Cheese: best forecast of the futures error is 'Fitted share of (cash + seasonal) gap' (out-of-sample R² -1.0% vs the futures price, right on direction 48.2% of the time, month-clustered t -0.55).
Butter: best forecast of the futures error is 'Ridge: stocks, production, exports, use' (out-of-sample R² +2.2% vs the futures price, right on direction 58.6% of the time, month-clustered t 1.19).

Nonfat dry milk: best forecast of the futures error is 'Fitted share of the spot nowcast gap' (out-of-sample R² -7.0% vs the futures price, right on direction 48.3% of the time, month-clustered t -2.72).
Dry whey: best forecast of the futures error is 'Ridge: stocks, production, exports, use' (out-of-sample R² +1.5% vs the futures price, right on direction 55.2% of the time, month-clustered t 2.24).

Supply and demand (ERS stocks vs normal, production, exports, domestic use) forecast the next 3 months of announced prices with out-of-sample R² Class III milk -21%, Class IV milk -13%, Cheese -14%, Butter -8%, Nonfat dry milk -16%, Dry whey -28%; momentum alone: Class III milk -12%, Class IV milk -4%, Cheese -8%, Butter -8%, Nonfat dry milk -9%, Dry whey +10%.
